Q: NL-to-SQL pipeline with PostgreSQL — join path selection, reserved word errors, and query accuracy A:

For reserved word table names (or table names containing spaces or punctuation), delimit them in double-quotes.

For example:

SELECT * FROM "table";

Then you also have to account for table names that contain a literal double-quote. For example, if the table name were odd"name, delimit the table name and replace the single literal double-quote with two double-quotes:

SELECT * FROM "odd""name";

As for the LLM business, I have no suggestions.

In general, I think SQL is already a fine language and it's not necessary, beneficial, or a good use of your time to make a natural language to SQL converter.

Q: Understanding x86 calling conventions from a book to generated code A:

The architecture x86-64 is exactly the same as ADM64. In some contexts, these terms are interchangeable (x64 is also used sometimes). The architecture was developed by AMD as the extension of IA-32, and later embraced by Intel. It can be considered as a simplification of IA-64 (Itanium architecture), not compatible with AMD64.

Strictly speaking, calling conventions are based on the CPU architecture, but are not defined by it. Conventions are conventions. They are used for the compatibility with different high-level language compilers and may be used by the Assembly code or not. If the functions are used only internally, following the conventions is not a strict requirement.

The difference in the book/documentation you observe is just the problem of this documentation. I would use a high-level language compiler to see how different functions are implemented for different calling conventions.

Q: Change dash Checklist values by callback A:

There were some little mistakes that cause the problem I want to mention here:

  • There is no id for the dcc.Checklist in the code
  • There must be a return statement. In my case, there was no return defined
  • if n_clicks < 1 means the button must be clicked twice for something to happen. It should be n_clicks > 0

So the solution is:

import dash
import dash_core_components as dcc
import dash_html_components as html
from dash.dependencies import Input, Output

app = dash.Dash(__name__)

app.layout = html.Div(
    [
        dcc.Checklist(
            id="checklist",
            options=[
                {"label": "New York City", "value": "NYC"},
                {"label": "Montréal", "value": "MTL"},
                {"label": "San Francisco", "value": "SF"},
            ],
            labelStyle={"display": "block"},
            value=[],
        ),
        html.Button("load", id="load-button", n_clicks=0),
    ]
)


@app.callback(Output("checklist", "value"), Input("load-button", "n_clicks"))
def change_values(n_clicks):
    return ["SF"] if n_clicks > 0 else []

Thanks to AnnMarieW to find the mistakes on plotly forum! See the original post on the forum.

Q: SSRS date range parameter A:

Add a couple of parameters in SSRS say, FromDate and ToDate and make its data type as Date/Time. You can specify the default values for these parameters using DateAdd functions and samples give below:

Today: 

=Today()

last week from today:

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Day, -7,Today())

You can add/reduce year, quarter month etc. in a similar way as shown below. Just change the number to the required length

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Year,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Quarter,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Month,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.DayOfYear,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.WeekOfYear,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.WeekDay,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Hour,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Minute,-1,Today())

=DateAdd(DateInterval.Second,-1,Today())

Q: Submitting a Spark job using Shell script file A:

That error comes when you pass in a value with no matching pattern. You passed in rma but you didn't have a case for it. Just add this...

args(0) match  {
  case "str1" => TestQuery(spark).runstr1
  case "xyz" => TestQuery(spark).runxyz
  case "str2" => TestQuery(spark).runstr2
  case "str3" => TestQuery(spark).runstr3
  case _ => TestQuery(spark).someDefaultDefined
}
